longevitymap v2 — research report

Evidence-tiered, mechanism-first longevity genetics for just-dna-lite · built 2026-11-03 · numbers from this session's audit and literature tracks; tier counts provisional until curation

Overview

v2 rebuilds the module around genome-wide, replicated evidence, organised by how each variant acts, with seven per-locus axes reported separately and no summed per-SNP score. Full specification: longevitymap_v2_requirements.md.

Key principles

  1. Evidence first: only genome-wide, replicated signals are scored; everything else is research view.
  2. One lead variant per locus; LD proxies and APOE-region tags are never counted twice.
  3. A lead SNP “marks a region” unless fine-mapping makes it likely causal; name the gene only when confident.
  4. Say what it acts through, at what age, on healthy years or on length of life, and state trade-offs both ways.
  5. Every genotype gets a row; the most common genotype is the neutral reference.
  6. Ancestry, sex and age limits travel with the finding.
  7. Every claim has a receipt: PMID, effect allele, effect size with unit, located quote.

Never

  • A summed “longevity score” or net weight from single SNPs
  • A predicted lifespan or genotype-based “biological age”
  • Red/green good–bad colouring, least of all on trade-offs
  • Odds ratios for citizens without plain-language context
  • “Gene that controls ageing” wording
  • An animal result raising a human tier or weight

Why v2

v1.2.0 is a faithful port of HAGR LongevityMap, frozen at Build 3 (2017-06-24; Tacutu 2018, de 2024). Out of date is not broken: it met LongevityMap's contract, an inclusive literature index. Measured on 2026-11-03 (audit profile):

280 / 516study-cited rsIDs rest on one 2012 classifier (Sebastiani 2012); its 2010 predecessor is retracted (Sebastiani 2010)
975 / 1,022genotype rows labelled “protective”; 47 risk; 0 neutral
35 / 528rsIDs with ≥2 independent significant studies
79distinct conclusion texts for 1,022 rows; none addresses the reader
0 / 671study rows with effect allele, effect size or p-value
~7 / ~150genome-wide longevity rsIDs in v1 (provisional; trait-set dependent)

Missing entirely: LPA, CHRNA3/5, 9p21 (CDKN2B-AS1), SH2B3/ATXN2, HLA-DQA1/DRB1, LDLR, FURIN, ZW10 — the best-replicated modern loci (Timmers 2019, Deelen 2019, Timmers 2020, Joshi 2017).

Evidence tiers

Merged rubric from the methodology, GWAS, preprint and reporting tracks; labels follow ClinGen risk-allele language (Schmidt 2024) and Venice credibility grading (Ioannidis 2008).

A · Well establishedp < 5×10⁻⁸ for longevity / lifespan / parental lifespan / healthspan in ≥100k lives or ≥3k cases above the 90th percentile; independent replication, same allele and direction; no red-flag heterogeneity. Shown first.
B · Likelygenome-wide locus but one study, a tag SNP outside the credible set, a much smaller replicated effect, or ancestry-specific replication only. Shown.
C · Early evidencesuggestive (p < 10⁻⁵), small or same-group replication, preprint only. Research view.
D · Not supportedcandidate-only without adequate replication, contradicted (e.g. IL6, USP42, TMTC2 in Timmers 2019), meta-null, retracted or overfit source. Research view, as negative evidence.

Hard rules: rows supported only by PMID 22279548 → D; unreplicated centenarian-vs-young designs capped at C; European tiers not transferred to other ancestries; MR-only, sub-genome-wide and n = 1 genomes never A/B.

Seed tiers are a mechanical consensus of track proposals; curation will prune tier B (many single-study GWAS Catalog hits).

Classification axes

Each scored locus carries these axes, reported separately and never merged into one score.

AxisValuesAnswersHome in format 0.7.1
Evidence tierA / B / C / Dgates scoring and default visibilityflags tier:X + priority (format request: evidence_tier)
Mechanismheart_vessels, brain_memory, smoking_lungs, immune_inflammation, metabolism, skin_sun, general_ageing, ageing_markerswhat the locus acts through; report groupingcategory; mediator EFO in flags
Pleiotropymech:<area>, broad, tradeoff, context:<x>, nonadditive, ap:<strength>, mr:drug_target_proxytrade-offs both waysflags (+ reserved pleiotropic); negatives prose; direction=contested
Age of actionlifelong / midlife / late / age_inverting / early_life / unknownwhen in life the effect operatesflags age:<class>; evidence in studies.csv
Outcome profilehealthspan · lifespan · exceptional survival: raises / none / lowers / untestedhealthy years vs length of life vs reaching very old ageflags outcome:<dim><sign>; phenotype class per study row
Actionabilitypreventable / modifiable / descriptive + what (test, screening, behaviour) + who (you / doctor)is there something to measure or changeactionability (closed vocab) + flags act_test:/act_behaviour:
Contexteur_only_evidence, ancestry_specific:<pop>, sex_specific:<m|f>who the evidence applies toflags; population on studies.csv
Causal / effector confidenceC1–C4 (fine-mapping PIP) · E1–E4 (L2G, coloc)is this SNP causal; which geneflags causal:/effector:; gene = effector call
Animal supportgenage_mouse, mouse_qtl, worm_rnaicross-species context onlyflags animal:; studies.csv model_organism

Worked example: LPA rs10455872

Tier A — genome-wide in parental lifespan (Timmers 2019; +0.76 years per A allele) and the multivariate scan (Timmers 2020)
Mechanism heart_vessels — Lp(a)-driven coronary disease and aortic stenosis
Pleiotropy mech:cvd; very low Lp(a) linked to type 2 diabetes (trade-off at the extreme)
Age of action MIDLIFE (confidence DIRECT_WEAK): per-allele log protection ratio 0.109 → 0.078 → 0.053 across parental ages 40–60 / 60–80 / 80+ (age moderation P = 0.04, FDR q = 0.76). Report phrase: “Mainly lowers the chance of dying before about 80, through less Lp(a)-driven heart and valve disease; the benefit shrinks but does not disappear at older ages.”
Outcome profile lifespan ✓ · healthspan ✓ (multivariate scan) · exceptional survival: to be checked against 90th/99th-percentile data at curation
Protection type PROTECT:ABSENCE_OF_RISK — the common allele does not raise Lp(a)
Actionability preventable — an Lp(a) blood test, once in life, ordered by a doctor; the measured level matters more than the genotype
Context eur_only_evidence — risk allele G ≈ 7% in non-Finnish Europeans, ≈ 0.1% in East Asians (gnomAD via Open Targets)
Causal / effector C2 (PIP 0.38; second signal rs186696265 PIP 0.93) · E1/E2 (L2G LPA 0.56–0.76)

Mechanism map

Most lifespan signal runs through specific diseases: in Timmers 2019 the top disease SNPs explain 0.43 y² of lifespan variance via CVD, 0.15 y² via smoking/lung cancer and 0.11 y² via other cancers; APOE alone 0.23 y². Tiers are seed consensus (provisional). ★ animal support · ⇄ trade-off.

preventable: Lp(a), LDL-C, blood pressure

Pleiotropy & age

From the pleiotropy track (Open Targets credible-set PheWAS + literature; locus table). Timmers 2020 (Timmers 2020): the protective effects of the 9 non-APOE loci shrink ~24% per decade of parental age while the APOE ε4 effect grows ~32% per decade — most loci act on mid- and late-life mortality, not on reaching extreme ages.

Age of action

Classes (40 loci, provisional): MIDLIFE: 18 · LIFELONG: 12 · UNKNOWN: 6 · LATE: 4. Confidence: DIRECT_WEAK: 21 · INFERRED: 9 · UNKNOWN: 6 · DIRECT: 4. No locus met AGE_INVERTING or EARLY_LIFE criteria. Source: age track (age_of_action.csv, synthesis). Parental-lifespan data censor late effects, so “mid-life” partly reflects that parents had to die for the effect to be seen.

Caveats from the track: allele labels in the source sheet do not always match the seed's pro-longevity allele (magnitudes shown in the lifespan-increasing direction; CDKN2B-AS1 orientation to be re-checked); three loci used unverified LD proxies; seven tier-B loci (TERT, IL6, IL6R, PCSK9, TCF7L2, IRF4, TYR) have no age-stratified lifespan data and are classed INFERRED or UNKNOWN.

Defining pro-longevity

Newer approaches, 2025–2026

Preprints flagged; most read at abstract level; PMIDs title-verified by the tracks.

approachwhat it defines as pro-longevityrepresentative work (PMID)main caveatuse in v2
Age-stratified / ancestry-specific survival GWASalleles whose association changes with the age band reached41949656; 42176242; Sasaki 2025 (preprint)small, suggestive; 3 of 14 replicated SNPs flipped direction (Taiwan)score only if tier rules met; ancestry-restricted

Approaches across the field (conceptual-reviews track)

approachdescriptionrepresentative_papers_pmidsstrengthsblind_spotsimplication_for_module
candidate-gene case-controlCentenarians/nonagenarians vs younger controls genotyped at hypothesis-driven SNPs (IIS, lipids, inflammation, antioxidants).35628444;16257164;18930842;22496539;28143747Cheap; biologically motivated; built most of HAGR LongevityMap.Small n; younger controls born decades later (cohort/birth-period confounding); ancestry mismatch; winner's curse; publication bias. Model-organism plausibility (e.g., SIRT1) often fails in humans; few loci beyond APOE/FOXO3 replicate.Most v1 rows. Downgrade single-study candidate rows by default; mark design in studies.csv; never present as established.
candidate-gene meta-analysisPooling published case-control studies per variant to obtain pooled ORs.29890178;25385258;23623925;36834822;24589462;23977315;18930842;20362697;24350933;30633899;28143747Gives pooled OR+CI; exposes heterogeneity and null results (PON1, IL6 overall).Inherits biased inputs; phenotype and control definitions differ; can inflate false negatives or bias estimates; sex/ancestry subgroup findings (FOXO3 males, IL6 Italian males, CETP direction flip) are fragile.Use pooled ORs for the few meta-analysed variants (APOE, ACE, FOXO3, CETP, KL, IL6) in effect_size/effect_measure. Encode nulls as non-protective states with a 'replication_failed' or 'meta_null' flag.
extreme-longevity GWAS (survival-percentile thresholds)Cases defined as surviving beyond the 90th/99th (or top 1%) birth-cohort survival percentile; controls ≤60th percentile.31413261;28329165;36613555;28977569;30060062Birth-cohort-standardised phenotype; separates extreme-survival variants from mortality-selection artefacts.Very limited power (thousands of cases); few genome-wide hits (APOE, GPR78 region, CDKN2B-AS1); ancestry-restricted.Record the percentile threshold per claim (studies.csv). APOE ε2/ε4 are the robust anchors. Report 'odds of reaching ≥90th/99th percentile', not 'lifespan years'.
parental-lifespan GWAS (proxy phenotype)GWAS of genotyped participants against their parents' age at death/attained age (UK Biobank, LifeGen).29030599;29227965;30642433;34704651Huge n (≈1M parental lifespans); many replicated loci; enables MR and PGS.Proxy dilutes effect by ~half (one parent shares 50% of alleles); dominated by disease and behaviour loci (APOE, LPA, CHRNA3/5 smoking, CDKN2B-AS1); European-centric; tells about mid-late-life mortality more than extreme longevity.Label phenotype 'parental lifespan' distinctly. Expect such loci to be disease-mediated; cross-link to disease modules instead of double counting.
healthspan and multivariate ageing GWASHealthspan (age at first chronic disease), or genetic factors combining healthspan, lifespan, longevity, frailty, self-rated health (mvAge, aging-GIP1).30729179;32678081;37550455;37118362Boosts power; captures shared ageing biology; discovers new loci (SLC4A7, haem metabolism; LPA/VCAM1).Composite traits are hard to interpret per-allele; heavy UK Biobank/European overlap; effect sizes not on a lifespan scale.Allow phenotype values healthspan/multivariate_ageing. Treat as separate evidence lines from 'extreme longevity'.
familial longevity scoring and family designsLRC, FLoSS and ancestral-longevity counts to select heritable longevity cases; sib-pair linkage; offspring-of-centenarian designs.30617297;32352215;37500622;34739053;34929024;42646838;41427385Removes phenocopies; shows longevity is transmitted from top-10% survivors and ≥20% long-lived relatives; offspring show compression of morbidity.Family-specific rare variants rarely replicate; familial advantage fades by ~100 years; data mainly European/US.README should state that a family history of longevity carries information that genotype rows do not capture. Optional user input (family history) is out of scope for genotype-only scoring.
heritability estimationTwin, pedigree and population-tree estimates, corrected for assortative mating or extrinsic mortality.30401766;29496957;41610249;41610247;34739053Bounds what genetics can explain.Estimates span <10% (assortative-mating corrected pedigrees) to >50% (intrinsic mortality, 2026); they depend on cohort era and how extrinsic death is handled; not individual-level.README: present the range and the 2026 debate. Never imply an individual's lifespan is X% genetic.
disease-risk-allele burden / absence of riskCompare GWAS disease risk allele counts or PRS (AD, CAD, T2D, cancer) between long-lived and controls.20921414;25664523;32860726;27114037;38634500;40615639;42065824;37605876;35754110Tests whether longevity = absence of risk. Shows mixed answer: overall burden similar, but AD and CAD risk depleted in the healthiest/longest-lived.Depends on which PRS; trade-offs (higher SCZ/T2D PRS in Chinese centenarians); small centenarian samples.Link variant rows to disease PGS rather than re-encoding disease alleles as 'longevity' alleles. Report: 'long-lived people carry many risk alleles too'.
rare / loss-of-function variant burden (WES/WGS)Exome/genome sequencing of centenarians, supercentenarians and biobanks; gene burden tests.32254024;37117740;39424787;37117627;40021682;40232348;25390934;33941312;36215696;38301647;32860726Identifies protective rare alleles (SIRT6, IIS/AMPK, mTOR genes) and lifespan-shortening LoF (BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2).Rare variants are mostly family- or population-private; burden signals are gene-level not variant-level; CH contaminates blood-derived calls (TET2, ASXL1, DNMT3A).Gene-level burden cannot be a variants.csv row. Use README/gene notes. Flag CH genes as possibly somatic. Defer BRCA1/2/ATM to ACMG modules.
buffering, conditional and age-dependent effectsGenotype frequency trajectories across ages; buffered-deleterious genotypes; antagonistic pleiotropy and age-sign-flipping effects.22496539;26306600;32130932;42020758;42481894;40680229;28977569Explains why risk alleles persist in centenarians and why effects invert with age.Hard to estimate; few human datasets with dense age bins; mouse evidence dominates age-inversion.Add flag 'age_dependent_effect' / 'conditional_on_genotype' (e.g., MTP buffered by other genotypes; Wnt variants in APOE4 carriers).
polygenic longevity scoresWeighted sums of lifespan/longevity GWAS variants (PLS, iLGS, longevity PRS).30642433;33216869;38451433;39198552;40680229;32251405;38684374Shows ~4-5 year differences between extreme deciles; partly offsets APOE ε4.Small per-person predictive value (HR ~0.7–1.2; time-dependent); European training data; sensitive to population structure.Point to PGS Catalog entries via the pgs table, not to an ad-hoc sum of variants.csv weights. Report deciles with uncertainty.
Mendelian randomization (risk factor, drug target, omics)Genetic instruments for exposures, proteins, CpGs, gene expression tested against lifespan/longevity.29030599;33704808;37118362;37550455;34704651;35078808;31444995;31552141;38243142Prioritises causal modifiable factors (LDL/PCSK9, BMI, BP, IL6R, LPA, VCAM1) and causal CpGs.Pleiotropy; survival bias; European instruments; tells population average causal effects, not individual predictions.Add a flag such as 'mr_supported' for rows where the locus' mediator has MR support. Show it as the actionable layer in the report (modifiable exposures).
omics ageing clocks (proteomic, metabolomic, epigenetic, organ-specific)Machine-learned biological-age predictors from plasma proteins, metabolites, methylation; organ-specific clocks.39117878;38057571;40634782;41299092;39504246;33512769;31431621;34187551;42162380;38355974;37657418Measurable, modifiable, and strongly predictive of mortality; may capture resilience to APOE4.Not genotype-derived; platform-specific; validation incomplete; correlation not causation (except causal clocks).Out of scope for genotype rows. README pointer: genotype is weaker than measured biomarkers; avoid implying genetic 'biological age'.
exposome + polygenic integrationExposome-wide association plus PRS to partition mortality variance; PRS × lifestyle joint effects.39972219;38684374;29030599Quantifies the small share of mortality explained by common genetics (<2 pp) vs exposome (17 pp).Observational exposome; UKB volunteer bias; European.Report must contextualise: lifestyle effects (HR ~1.8) exceed genetic predisposition (HR ~1.2) and are additive.
pathway / hallmark / network aggregationGrouping loci into conserved pathways or hallmarks; interactome modules; co-expression enrichment of GWAS signals.37941149;36599349;34271186;42362889;39778705;30642433Interpretable grouping; links weak single-SNP signals to biology; consistent five pathways (IIS, DDR, immunity, cholesterol, telomeres).Hallmarks are not causal paradigms; gene-set enrichment is not per-variant evidence; risk of circularity with model-organism priors.Replace v1 'other' (483/1022 rows) with a controlled pathway vocabulary in category. Display grouping only; no pathway-sum score.
evolutionary / comparative genomicsLong-lived species genomes (bowhead, naked mole-rat, rockfish, beaver), convergent evolution, cross-species transcriptomes; functional tests in human cells.25565328;41162698;41066557;34297086;36630509;32726638;37269831;34762458;42115756;40997294Nominates mechanisms (DNA repair, CIRBP, cGAS, aryl-hydrocarbon metabolism) and gene sets enriched in human lifespan heritability.Species-specific substitutions are almost never polymorphic in humans (81.2% invariant; 99.78% <1%); cannot become genotype rows.Gene-level 'comparative support' annotation (README or a gene-level side table). No variants.csv rows from species data.
somatic mutation and mosaicismClonal haematopoiesis, mosaic chromosomal alterations, somatic mutation rates across species and tissues.35418684;38490496;36988570;37117740;40021682;33184493;40997805;40604182;42240775Explains TET2/ASXL1/DNMT3A lifespan signals; centenarians carry fewer mCAs.Somatic burden is not germline; generally weak evidence as a driver of ageing (except cancer); needs VAF-aware calling.Flag CH-gene variants with low VAF as 'possible_somatic'; module output should say germline-only interpretation is assumed.
long-read structural variant and repeat analysisNanopore/PacBio genomes resolving SVs, VNTRs, telomere length.41282933;34155099;38890274Recovers >60% of SVs missed by short reads; VNTRs (TERT) linked to centenarian status.Early, small, preprint-level for ageing; not yet longevity-GWAS scale.Use requires_callable/callable_from for indel/repeat variants (e.g., ACE I/D); mark 'not assessable from short-read/array' in report.
AI / machine learningVariant-effect predictors (AlphaMissense), LLM biological age, AI target discovery, AI-assisted meta-analysis.37733863;40702324;35347083;31845988;36834822;41685266Scales annotation; prioritises rare missense variants; new biological-age proxies.Pathogenicity is not longevity effect; most ageing-AI lacks validation (3% in vivo).Optional computed annotation column for missense rare variants (score source + version). Never use as association evidence.
N-of-1 deep phenotyping of extreme agersMulti-omics of individual supercentenarians and the world's oldest person.40997805;33184493;25390934;42240775Hypothesis-generating; shows CH, telomere attrition coexist with health.n=1; not generalisable.No rows. Cite only in README as context.

Systematic comparison of definitions

definitionstudy_phenotype_classwhat_it_detectsblind_spots_biasesrepresentative_pmidsloci_foundrecommended_use_in_v2
a) Extreme-survival case-control (>=85/90/95 y, 90th/99th percentile, centenarians vs younger controls)EXTREME_SURVIVAL_CCAlleles whose frequency differs between survivors to a high age and younger/never-long-lived controls; integrates all mortality up to the threshold; strongest single-variant signals at the 99th percentile (Deelen 2019).Small case numbers (thousands); controls are often alive younger people, so variants acting before the control age are invisible and cohort/birth-year allele drift confounds; cannot say at what age the variant acted; centenarian selection mixes "absence of risk" with true protection; ancestry-specific (APOE/F31413261;24688116;25199915;22279548;28329165;36613555;30060062;18765803;19196970;26912274;41949656;41116190APOE e4/e2, FOXO3, 5q33.3 (rs2149954), GPR78, CDKN2A/B (99th, suggestive), IL6 rs2069837 and ANKRD20A9P (Han Chinese), HLA-DRB1*15:01 (male), ZNF806/NUAK1 etc. (Taiwan)SCORE (primary). Store percentile threshold and control age in studies.csv; weight 99th-percentile evidence as the most specific "longevity" signal.
b) Parental-lifespan / family-proxy GWAS (kin-cohort, Martingale residuals, parents' attained age, both parents top 10%)PARENTAL_LIFESPANPer-allele effect on parental hazard (years of life per allele, x2 to convert to self); very large N (~1M parents) gives most of the 20-30 known loci; age-band stratification possible (Timmers 2019 bands; Joshi 2016 <75 vs >=75).Parents dying <40 excluded and many parents still alive (right-censored), so late effects are underpowered (e.g., 1,853 paternal deaths at 90-120 y vs 84,545 at 70-80 y in Timmers 2019 source data); effect diluted by 50% kinship; cohort effects of parents born early 20th century (smoking era inflates CHRNA3/5); misr27029810;29030599;27015805;29227965;30642433;28748955;31484785;28092683APOE, CHRNA3/5, CDKN2B-AS1, LPA, HLA-DQA1/DRB1, SH2B3/ATXN2, FURIN/FES, ZW10, PSORS1C3, 13q21.31, ABO, ZC3HC1, IGF2R, LDLR, CELSR2/PSRC1, MAGI3, KCNK3, HTT, FOXO3, 5q33.3, MC2R (top-10% only), EPHX2SCORE (primary). Always flag PROXY:PARENTAL; record age bands where available; treat as weaker evidence for LATE effects.
c) Own-survival hazard (Cox) in prospective cohorts / biobanksOWN_SURVIVALHR for death in genotyped individuals; can test age interactions directly and censor intermediate diseases (Wolters 2019: e4 HR 1.17 attenuated to 1.07 after censoring dementia).Few deaths in biobanks recruited at 40-70 (UKB 35,551 deaths in Park 2025), so signals are dominated by early, cancer-driven deaths; follow-up covers a narrow age window; healthy-volunteer bias; disease-specific survival loci barely overlap susceptibility loci (Yang 2025).21782286;40021682;32251405;31356640;24497847;41028524;30060062APOE, ZSCAN23 (common); BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2, ASXL1, CKMT1B (LoF burden, life-shortening); PRS for SBP and BMISCORE (supporting); preferred source for age-interaction claims and for LIFELONG classification.
d) Healthspan / disease-free survival and multivariate ageing factors (healthspan GWAS, MANOVA, aging-GIP1, mvAge genomic SEM)HEALTHSPAN / MULTIVARIATE_AGEINGLoci shared by healthspan, lifespan, longevity, frailty, self-rated health and clocks; more power than any single trait; finds non-disease loci (FOXO3, FGD6, ZW10, SLC4A7, LINC02513, HTT, MAML3).Healthspan = first of a list of diseases (Zenin: 7 conditions incl. cancer) so it counts non-fatal events (skin cancer, pigmentation loci IRF4/TYR/DEF8) and is censored at UKB ages (<~80); composite factors inherit the inputs' sample overlap and weighting; a factor locus need not affect lifespan; frailty/self-r30729179;32678081;37118362;37550455;30962613;21782286Zenin: APOE, LPA, HLA class II (rs1049053), IRF4, TYR, DEF8, FGFR2, CDKN2B-AS1...; Timmers 2020: FOXO3, SLC4A7, LINC02513, ZW10, FGD6, LPA, LDLR, CDKN2B-AS1, TOX3, APOE; aging-GIP1: 27 regions incl. HTT, MAML3; mvAge: 38 loci incl. TCF7L2, PABPC4SCORE only when the locus also has a lifespan-type signal (a, b or c) at least suggestive; otherwise ANNOTATE with label HEALTHSPAN_ONLY.
e) Age-dependent allele-frequency change in cross-sectional cohorts (viability selection)VIABILITY_AFAlleles whose frequency declines with age among the living or with parental age at death; intrinsically gives an age-of-action profile (e4 decline from ~70 y; CHRNA3 decline across all paternal ages).Confounded by birth-cohort ancestry drift and recruitment bias (needs ancestry/batch null model); power depends on where the change occurs (Mostafavi: ~20/90/60% power for change starting at 20/50/70 y); only very large effects reach genome-wide significance (only APOE and CHRNA3 found).28873088;31484785APOE e4 (rs6857, rs769449), CHRNA3 (rs1051730), MEOX2 rs4721453 (sensitivity analysis); trait-PGS signals (puberty timing, cholesterol, CAD, BMI, asthma)SCORE (supporting/confirmatory) and PRIMARY SOURCE for age_of_action; never sole evidence.
f) Familial longevity scores (FEL, LRC/mLRC) and long-lived families (LLS, LLFS)FAMILIAL_LONGEVITYHeritable longevity: transmitted only when top-10% survivors cluster (>=20% of relatives long-lived); selects cases with less phenocopy; family members have >10 y delayed first chronic disease.Is a case-selection device rather than a variant test; small samples; requires multigeneration genealogy; enriched for specific populations (Utah, Netherlands, Ashkenazi); results feed back into (a) or (g).11253150;30617297;32352215;33407157;42065824Few single loci; LLS: lower CAD PGS and cholesterol-metabolism PGSANNOTATE (study design attribute in studies.csv); evidence from such studies is scored under EXTREME_SURVIVAL_CC with a FAMILIAL flag that up-weights specificity.
g) Depletion of disease-risk alleles / low polygenic disease burden in the long-livedDISEASE_DEPLETIONWhether long-lived people simply lack common disease risk alleles ("absence of risk"); informed scans (iGWAS, Bayesian priors) boost power using disease GWAS.Results conflict by disease and design: no global depletion for CAD/cancer/T2D alleles in Leiden nonagenarians (Beekman 2010) and no pathogenic-variant depletion in Ashkenazi centenarians (Gutman 2020), but CAD PGS lower with more long-lived ancestors (Sant'Anna 2026), AD protective PGS higher in centenarians (Bae20921414;42065824;27114037;26677855;28748955;27015805;33216869;40615639;32860726Mainly polygenic (CAD, AD, SBP, BMI, cholesterol); single loci only via informed scans (CDKN2B-AS1, ATXN2/SH2B3, LPA ...)ANNOTATE (label ABSENCE_OF_RISK); do not create new pro-longevity rows from disease GWAS alone - route to disease modules.
h) Rare protective loss-of-function ("human knockouts") and gene-burden testsRARE_BURDENGene-level effects of PTV/missense burden on lifespan; rare protective alleles in centenarians (IGF1R, mTOR, IIS/AMPK, Wnt); drug-target-like LoF with lifelong biomarker lowering (PCSK9, LPA, APOC3).Large-N burden tests find mainly life-SHORTENING genes (BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2) driven by cancer and clonal haematopoiesis; pro-longevity rare variants come from small centenarian exomes and are unreplicated; protective LoF evidence is usually for disease, not lifespan; somatic CHIP mimics germline in blood-derived exomes.37117740;40021682;32254024;37117627;40232348;18316725;16554528;28406212;28007139;32860726;27114037Shortening: BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, TET2, ASXL1, CKMT1B; candidate protective: IGF1R, RPS6, FLCN, SIK3, RWDD1, Wnt-pathway genes; disease-protective LoF: PCSK9, LPA, APOC3ANNOTATE for pro-longevity rare variants (tier C-D unless replicated); life-shortening burden genes belong in disease modules (negatives/cross-links).
i) Evolutionary / selection-based (antagonistic pleiotropy, mutation accumulation, balancing selection, comparative genomics)EVOLUTIONARYWhy risk alleles persist (early-life fitness benefit, late cost); predicts which loci should be trade-offs and age-specific; comparative constraint across mammals.Not a variant-level test of human lifespan; population-genetic signals are confounded by demography; comparative genomics works at gene level; many claims rest on single cohorts (Ghana APOE fertility).28812720;38064565;28640878;31863128;32043462;28683096;23094790APOE e4 (fertility/infection), CAD loci with reproductive pleiotropy, reproduction PGSANNOTATE only (pleiotropy label AP; supports TRADEOFF and AGE_INVERTING hypotheses).
j) Causal / Mendelian-randomization definitions (variant as proxy for a modifiable mediator)MR_MEDIATORVariants whose lifespan effect is explained by a causal risk factor (LDL, Lp(a), BP, BMI, smoking, education, VCAM1); defines actionability.A pro-longevity allele here is "lower exposure"; horizontal pleiotropy; MR assumes lifelong linear effects so says nothing about age at action; weak instruments for protein targets.29030599;32251405;37118362;37550455;28748955;16554528;28007139LPA/apo(a), VCAM1, LDLR, PCSK9, CELSR2/SORT1, CHRNA3/5 (smoking), BP and BMI PGSANNOTATE (modifiable_mediator, actionability); allows the score of a locus to be qualified but not created.
k) Biomarker-anchored (slower epigenetic/proteomic clock, telomere length)BIOMARKER_CLOCKVariants associated with slower biological-age measures; large N; mechanistic hypotheses (TERT, GDF15).Clock acceleration is not lifespan: TERT telomere-lengthening alleles raise IEAA (Lu 2018); clocks capture smoking/adiposity/SES; proteomic clocks are dominated by exposome; direction can conflict with mortality.29374233;34187551;39972219;33948810;14559957TERT (IEAA), ~137 DNAm-clock loci; CDKN2A/B rs2184061 (GDF15 signature); CETP I405V (lipoprotein size)ANNOTATE only (BIOMARKER label); never contributes to pro-longevity score.

Rare variants & animals

Animal evidence

GenAge mouse lifespan genes overlap 22 of 272 v1 genes by NCBI orthologues (20 by symbol; 26 with Open Genes) but only 3 of 71 genes at GWAS-era loci (TERT, APOE, HTT): knockout-style animal evidence and human genome-wide evidence barely overlap. Unbiased mouse population genetics is the bridge: UM-HET3 (3,276 genotyped ITP mice; Bou 2022), Diversity Outbred (Mullis 2025, Mullis 2026, Di 2024) and BXD (Roy 2021). FGD6 is the cleanest cross-species case: human multivariate healthspan/lifespan locus rs12830425 (Timmers 2020) and a late-life mouse lifespan QTL candidate whose worm orthologue shortens lifespan when knocked down.

Allele-level and direction checks (model-organism re-run)

  • Almost no human longevity allele has been tested allele-specifically in mice with a lifespan endpoint. The only knock-in found with lifespan data is PPARG Pro12Ala (Ala/Ala longer-lived on chow; benefit lost on a high-fat diet; PMID 19117549, title-verified by the track). Humanised Klotho variant knock-ins exist only as conference abstracts; no FOXO3 rs2802292, SIRT6 N308K/A313S or IGF1R A37T/R407H knock-in lifespan study was found.
  • Direction can disagree across species: Igf1r+/- mice (female +33%) are concordant with reduced-function IGF1R alleles in female centenarians; GHR knockout extends mouse life, while human d3-GHR raises GH sensitivity and is male-specific (discordant); KL-VS is non-monotone in humans (heterozygote advantage) but monotone in mice.
  • Corrected count: with NCBI orthologues, 22 of 272 v1 genes (45 rsIDs) have GenAge mouse lifespan entries (symbol matching gave 20); Open Genes adds to a union of 26 genes (51 rsIDs).
  • v1's KL rs1207362, IGF1R rs2229765 and SIRT6 rs107251 are not the functionally characterised alleles. Candidates instead: KL-VS (rs9536314 + rs9527025, as a haplotype), d3-GHR tag rs6873545, BPIFB4 rs2070325 — identities to be verified at curation.
  • The SIRT6 centenarian-allele paper (Simon 2022) is in EMBO J (PMID 36215696), not Cell Reports as the brief said.

Rare and protective variants

  • Centenarian sequencing is small and largely negative at variant level: WES of 100 centenarians found no rare-variant or gene burden (PMID 29750252); WGS 81 vs 36 gave STK17A/COA1 plus a DNA-repair signal (PMID 33941312); ClinVar/HGMD pathogenic burden did not differ among 1,879 Ashkenazi centenarians, offspring and controls (PMID 32860726).
  • APOE is the only replicated direct-lifespan locus at this level (28,297 participants, 7 studies; PMID 30060062). FOXO3 rs2802292 is meta-analytically significant in men but null in Japanese and Italian samples; d3-GHR rises with age in 3 of 4 cohorts (men); CLEC3B rs13963 is East Asian-only; KL-VS acts as an Alzheimer's-risk modifier in APOE4 carriers.
  • Lipid loss-of-function (PCSK9, APOC3, ANGPTL3, ASGR1) protects against coronary disease (e.g. ANGPTL3 OR 0.59; APOC3 LoF −41% ischaemic vascular disease), but lifespan evidence is Mendelian randomisation only (PMID 38082436). APOE3-Christchurch and RELN-COLBOS delay Alzheimer's onset in single kindreds.
  • Pathogenic carriage shortens life: UK Biobank ACMG SF v3.2 P/LP carriers (3.4%) have all-cause mortality HR 1.42 (women) / 1.31 (men); PTV burden HR BRCA2 2.57, BRCA1 2.36, TET2 1.76, ATM 1.65. No “years lost” figure was found.
  • Germline clonal-haematopoiesis loci (TERT, TCL1A) act indirectly; CHIP itself carries all-cause mortality HR 1.34 (meta-analysis) and is not callable from a germline VCF. mtDNA haplogroup evidence is weak and unreplicated.
  • ADARB1/2 (18 v1 rsIDs) have no replication since 2015 → tier C.

Report design

Citizen scientist (default)

  • the result in plain words, about you
  • copies of the longer-life version (0, 1, 2)
  • certainty word; what it acts through; at what age
  • healthy years vs length of life
  • “may lower / may raise” for trade-offs
  • what a doctor can measure instead
  • ancestry caveat when it applies

Geneticist (More details)

  • rsID, GRCh38 position, ref/alt, zygosity
  • effect allele, effect size with unit, CI, p
  • phenotype class, cohort N and ancestry
  • fine-mapping and effector-gene confidence
  • located quotes and PMIDs

Ageing researcher (research view)

  • tiers C/D, negative and contradicted evidence
  • legacy LongevityMap rows (frozen 2017)
  • full pleiotropy list, hallmark tags
  • animal-model support

Context card (always shown)

  • “Most of how long people live is not explained by known DNA variants.” (Bian 2024, Argentieri 2025)
  • Heritability depends on the estimand: <10% after correcting for assortative mating (Ruby 2018); 12–16% in large family trees (Kaplanis 2018); ~50% for “intrinsic” lifespan, contested (Shenhar 2026).
  • “Long-lived people carry many disease-risk variants too.” (Beekman 2010)
  • “Nothing here predicts your lifespan.”

Wording rules

  • Open with the reader's result; association wording; size in words; certainty ladder = tier.
  • No rsID, p-value, OR or coordinate in labels or conclusions.

  • Trade-offs get a two-sided sentence and no good/bad colour.

Build plan & decisions

  1. Scaffold spec (name longevitymap, 2.0.0, GRCh38; weighting, licence, defaults)
  2. Curate lead loci from the seed: confirm tiers, one lead per locus, harmonise the lifespan-increasing allele (target ~25–40 scored loci)
  3. Evidence: effect numbers from paper tables/supplements, verbatim quotes, sign conventions resolved (Timmers years +, Pilling Martingale +=shorter, Zenin hazard +=worse)
  4. Enrich coordinates and ref checks (strand errors were v1's dominant repair)
  5. GWAS effects + fine-mapping (enrich_gwas_effects; Open Targets PIP/L2G as flags)
  6. Cross-check → compile --strict → verify
  7. Reviews: lay reader + scientific reviewer on the rendered report
  8. Trial install on the two public genomes (on request) → polygon rehearsal → publish on explicit yes

Consumer (just-dna-lite) and format requests

  • Category prose from the module or a report: block, replacing hardcoded LONGEVITY_CATEGORIES; hide Net weight; render negatives and flag chips; research-view toggle; “not screened” state; ancestry banner; link to PRS tab.
  • Format: evidence_tier column; associations/pleiotropy table; effect_modifiers table; second (mediator) EFO; fine-mapping fields on gwas_effects; allele-level HLA.

Limits

  • Rare-variant and mouse tracks were stopped by a content-safety filter on the first model and completed on a re-run with Sonnet 5.5, with the original briefs unchanged.
  • Age of action: no genome-wide age-varying-hazard lifespan GWAS exists; classes rest on Timmers 2019/2020 age bands and inference from mediating disease; provisional.
  • Mouse: GenAge-only rows lack paper-verified PMIDs; worm/fly matches symbol-only; positional synteny of mouse QTL with human loci not done.
  • Most per-study facts come from abstracts plus GWAS Catalog records; full texts read for Deelen 2019, Timmers 2019/2020, Joshi 2017 and the mouse papers. Budovsky 2013 full text not accessible.
  • GWAS Catalog queried for 6–8 trait IDs without child-term expansion; the ~150 genome-wide-rsID figure is provisional.
  • bioRxiv listing partial (49,792 of 130,451 records); medRxiv complete.
  • Open Genes and HALL data licences unverified (sites blocked in the sandbox).
  • Seed tiers are a mechanical consensus; single-track A calls need curator confirmation.
